question: Can the Commission inspect a company over conduct a national authority has already investigated? What limits apply, and how have the courts treated the overlap?
question_parts: Can the Commission inspect a company over conduct a national authority has already investigated?
How have the courts treated the overlap?

conclusion_first.reason: Answer opens with claim 1, an analytical point, not a conclusion addressing all three parts of the question.

parts_answered.reason: Part 1 answered by claim 12, part 2 by claims 2, 3, 5, 8, 10, and part 3 by claims 9, 11, 12.

tests_as_conditions.reason: The ne bis in idem test (claim 5) and Article 11(6) devolution test (claim 3) are stated in prose without ordered conditions or cumulation noted.

authorities_labelled.reason: Claim 6 correctly labels the Nordzucker source as an Advocate General's Opinion and no rule rests on it alone.

citations_complete.reason: All 12 claims cite filenames (e.g. 62013CJ0583.md, 62019CJ0857.md) without dates, ECLI or paragraph numbers as flagged in pre-checks.

no_duplicate_authorities.reason: Regulation 1/2003 is invoked repeatedly (claims 3, 4, 10) and C-857/19 is cited twice (claims 3 and 5) for related but distinct points.

no_off_topic.reason: Claim 4 on the ECN work-allocation mechanism describes a policy tool without directly answering any of the three question parts.

no_contradictions.reason: Claims 11 and 12 (prior proceedings don't bar inspection) sit consistently with claims 2, 9, 10 (limits on using tainted evidence).

currency_flagged.reason: No claim states the date as of which the law is given, and none of the cases are checked for supersession despite citing pre- and post-2019 rulings.

parts_answered.part: Can the Commission inspect a company over conduct a national authority has already investigated?
parts_answered.reason: Claim 12 directly holds an inspection is not inappropriate merely because a national authority already examined the conduct.
Claims 2, 3, 5, 8 and 10 set out limits: purpose limitation, loss of national competence, ne bis in idem, sufficient indicia, and recording obligations.

parts_answered.part: How have the courts treated the overlap?
parts_answered.reason: Claims 9, 11 and 12 show courts examining lawfulness of earlier inspections and rejecting automatic bars from prior proceedings.

verdict: 8/18 — Substantively covers all three parts with relevant case law but lacks an upfront conclusion, proper citation detail (dates/ECLI/paragraphs), ordered test structure, and date-stamping of the law, undermining reliability.
